subject: Data governance Q&A and next steps for Medigen private deployment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Lopez <ana.lopez@medigen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call: quick recap + info request (PII, retention, egress)

Hi Ana — thanks again for today’s discovery call. Quick recap and the pieces we need to move the private/VPC pilot forward: 

What we heard from Medigen (confirm if anything missing):
- EU data residency required for production workloads.
- PII scope: patient name, DOB, national id, and clinical identifiers flagged as regulated.
- Audit/logging retention: regulatory team expects immutability and 7-year retention for audit logs; access logs for 90 days is OK for some services but request is 7 years for forensic records.
- Dev environment is planned to be air-gapped; prod can accept restricted egress to approved endpoints.

What we’ll provide next: 
1) A concise Private deployment diagram showing network boundaries and egress controls (attached).
2) SOC2 summary and how Redwood's audit logs map to your retention ask (attached).
3) Options for connectivity: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs VPN + guidelines for IP allowlists.

Requests / next steps for Medigen: 
- Can you share a high-level network diagram showing where inference requests originate (VPC, on-prem) and any proxy/fabric in front? (Tom from infra would be ideal to include).
- Confirm if HSM/KMS integration is required for keys at rest and whether you have a preferred KMS vendor.
- Please attach the security questionnaire and any required evidence items; we’ll prioritize answers.

I’ve attached our private architecture + SOC2 summary to start. Proposed follow-up: a 60-minute technical alignment call with Tom and your infra/security folks — are you available Thursday or Friday afternoon CET?

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Ana Lopez <ana.lopez@medigen.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medigen.com, Tom Berger <tom.berger@medigen.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T10:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: quick recap + info request (PII, retention, egress)

Thanks Karthik — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from security and infra side: 

PII + residency: production data must remain in EU regions only. For the pilot we can use a single EU VPC. PII fields we treat as regulated include patient name, DOB, national identifier, and a couple of clinical codes — we’ll send a list in the questionnaire.

Retention: our compliance lead requires immutable audit logs for 7 years. Application request traces can be short-lived (90 days) but anything tied to patient records/forensics must be retained longer.

Egress / air-gap: dev teams are fully air-gapped and cannot reach public endpoints. Production is allowed limited egress but only to pre-authorised IPs or a private peering endpoint. We prefer peering/PrivateLink over NAT egress for sensitive traffic.

KMS: yes, we require customer-managed keys in our KMS (we use Keyshield Enterprise). We need proof that Redwood can support KMS integration or an HSM-backed key store.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire (medigen-security-q1.xlsx) and a simple network sketch for the pilot. Tom is looped to set up the technical call — he prefers Friday 14:00 CET.

Best,
Ana

Attachments: medigen-security-q1.xlsx

Subject: Re: Post-call: quick recap + info request (PII, retention, egress)

Hi Ana — looping in a few technical options and clarifying items from the Redwood infra side. Short answers up-front: we can support EU-only residency, customer-managed KMS (via standard KMS integration or HSM-backed options), and per-customer egress control. 

Connectivity options (tradeoffs):
- VPC Peering (recommended when you control both VPCs): low-latency, no public egress, but requires IP management and route table work on both sides.
- AWS PrivateLink / Private Endpoint: best for restricting access to specific services; removes need for NAT but requires endpoint creation in your VPC.
- IP allowlist / NAT egress: simplest for pilot but not ideal for strict residency/air-gap constraints.
- Air-gapped on-prem: possible for isolated dev stacks via offline model packaging; prod traffic would still require a secure import/export process, or a scheduled sync over a controlled tunnel.

Logging & retention: we can configure append-only audit logs and export copies to your S3 (EU) or to a customer-owned logging bucket. We support object immutability flags (WORM) if you need tamper-resistant storage for the 7-year window. Access auditing to logs can be scoped to roles.

Action items (proposed):
- Medigen: share the detailed network diagram (Tom) and the list of PII fields for scoping (Ana) — owner: Medigen; due: 2027-07-13.
- Redwood (Lauren): produce a VPC connectivity options brief and an implementation plan for PrivateLink + KMS integration — owner: Lauren; due: 2027-07-15.
- Redwood (Karthik): schedule 60-min technical alignment with Tom + security — proposed: Fri 14:00 CET; invite sent when confirmed.

I’ve attached a short one-pager on egress options (vpc-egress-options-onepager.pdf). If Friday 14:00 CET works, I’ll block the time and include our infra architects.

Thanks,
Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop | Solutions Architect
